fields.h1: Build Gym Automation for Memberships and Classes
fields.hero_description: Build gym automation that follows up on failed dues and alerts coaches when members stop checking in.
fields.features_heading: What Gym Automation Runs at the Desk
fields.features_subheading: Each workflow takes one job the front desk repeats and logs what it did on the member's record. Coaching stays with the coaches.
fields.feature_1:
Runs on a charge, a booking, or a scan

Reads failed charges from the payment processor's API and watches class bookings and the check-in screen. Each event starts a run, and the run is logged on the member's record.
fields.feature_2:
Gym rules in your front desk's words

Write a rule the way it gets said out loud at the desk, such as skip the dues reminder for anyone on a freeze. Emergent turns it into the workflow, and a new prompt changes it.
fields.feature_3:
Members, classes, and visits in one place

Keeps members, plans, class rosters, and every check-in in a database you own. Every workflow reads the same tables, and adding a class or a coach means adding one row.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts to the coach or manager on duty

Sends a Slack message or an email to the person who owns the next step. When nobody acts within a day, a reminder follows, and after that the item escalates to the gym manager.
fields.feature_5:
No task cap when sign-ups spike

Runs every charge, booking, and check-in through the same steps however many arrive. When a promotion doubles new members for a month, the extra runs go through with no task cap.
fields.feature_6:
Your gym app's code, yours to keep

Exports the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can read every rule written so far and connect another tool your gym uses through that tool's API.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Desk Jobs a Gym Can Hand Off
fields.tab_content_1:
Failed dues get two emails, then a flag at check-in

Halyard Barbell Club bills $64 monthly dues through Stripe. When Silvano Strout's card is declined, the app emails him for a new card on day 1 and again on day 4. On day 7, with the dues still unpaid, his profile shows a flag on the front desk check-in screen. Paying clears the flag.
fields.tab_content_2:
Canceled bikes move down the waitlist every 30 minutes

The 6:00 AM spin class holds 20 bikes, and 3 members are on the waitlist. At 4:40 AM Laszlo Wickstrom cancels bike 14, and the app emails it to Ozanne Peyton, first in line, with 30 minutes to claim it. Unclaimed at 5:10 AM, the offer moves to Marit Quillan. The roster updates when someone claims the bike.
fields.tab_content_3:
Members gone 14 days land on their coach's list

Every Monday at 8:00 AM the app finds members with no check-in for 14 days. Each coach gets their own names in a Slack direct message, with each member's last visit and usual class. Coach Florentyna Odell has 3 this week. She logs each call from the message, and a member leaves the list at their next check-in.
fields.tab_content_4:
Any trial with fewer than 2 visits in 5 days gets a call

A trial pass at Halyard runs 7 days and starts from a signup form on the gym's website. The app counts each trial member's check-ins. On day 5, anyone with fewer than 2 visits goes to Gideon Thackery, the front desk manager, in a Slack direct message. This week that is Esperanza Wickline, with 1 visit.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up gym automation for one front desk job, test it on last month's records, then add the next one.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the jobs the desk repeats
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick one job with a clear trigger
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down what the front desk does by hand in a normal week: chasing declined cards, moving people off class waitlists, calling members who stopped coming, and following up on trial passes. Note who does each job today and roughly how long it takes.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Choose the job that eats the most desk time and name the event that starts it, such as a declined card or a canceled booking. Then write its rule with real numbers: how many days, how many visits, and who gets told.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pull your member list, plans, class schedule, and coach assignments into one spreadsheet. Give every member a coach and every class a capacity. A workflow can only message the right coach when that column is filled in.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Tell Emergent what starts the workflow, which rule it applies, and who hears about it. Emergent builds the workflow, the screens the desk and coaches use, and the database behind them. A follow-up prompt changes any step.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Connect the payment processor, Slack, and email through their APIs. Send a test charge that fails on purpose, and confirm the member email and the check-in flag both appear. Then cancel a test booking to watch the waitlist offer go out.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run last month's declines, cancellations, and check-ins through the app before it messages anyone. Compare each result with what the desk actually did. Each mismatch points to a rule that needs a number changed, such as 10 days instead of 14.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Build the second workflow on the tables the first one already fills. Check-in records from the attendance list feed the trial pass count, and member records feed the dues follow-up. Each new workflow starts with less setup than the last.
fields.hero_prompt: Build gym automation for failed dues, class waitlists, attendance alerts, and trial passes.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up gym automation?

plan.angle: The top 10 are gym software vendors (Glofox, Club Automation, Gymdesk, Visual ClubMate) and Reddit threads that list billing, booking and CRM features without showing one rule an owner could switch on. This page shows four front-desk jobs at one independent gym, each with its trigger, its numbers and who hears about it: failed dues followed up on day 1 and day 4 and flagged at check-in on day 7, a canceled spin bike offered to the waitlist for 30 minutes at a time, members with no check-in for 14 days sent to their coach every Monday, and trial members with fewer than 2 visits by day 5 called by the front desk manager.
tab_stories: When a member's $64 dues payment fails in Stripe, the app emails them on day 1 and day 4, and if the dues are still unpaid on day 7 the front desk check-in screen shows a flag on their profile.

When Laszlo Wickstrom cancels his bike for the 6:00 AM spin class at 4:40 AM, the app offers bike 14 by email to Ozanne Peyton, first on the waitlist, and moves it to the next name if she has not claimed it in 30 minutes.
Every Monday at 8:00 AM the app finds members with no check-in for 14 days and sends each coach their own names in a Slack direct message, so coach Florentyna Odell gets 3 names to call.

A 7-day trial pass signed up on the website is tracked visit by visit, and any trial member with fewer than 2 visits by day 5 goes to front desk manager Gideon Thackery in a Slack direct message to call.
